stage_a.note: The founders are highly energetic and smiling while acting out a funny skit about the use case.
The presenting founder speaks with passion and clear excitement about the product's features.
The founders offer friendly greetings and maintain an approachable orientation toward the panel.

venture.description: A wearable and stickable Bluetooth remote with large buttons for controlling smartphone functions during activities.
venture.note: The product is designed to be used with gloves or wet hands.

turns.summary: The investor offers the requested 250,000 dollars for 10 percent equity, plus a 10 dollar royalty until 1 million is paid.

turns.summary: The founder points out that a 10 dollar royalty would take most of their 12 dollar profit per unit.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: The investor insists on his terms.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: An investor agrees that the founders cannot afford the proposed royalty.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder reiterates that a 10 dollar royalty is too much.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: An investor suggests that the founders make a counteroffer.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: The founder counters with a 2 dollar royalty instead of 10.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: An investor questions if they can even afford a 2 dollar royalty.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: The offering investor complains that a 2 dollar royalty would take too long to pay him back.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: An investor jokes about the offering investor's age.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder tries to negotiate by discussing their current inventory and sales potential.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: The offering investor maintains that it must be a 10 dollar royalty because it is just a product.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: An investor warns that a 10 dollar royalty will bankrupt the company.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: The offering investor argues their acquisition cost will drop after being on the show, making it affordable.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: The founder asks if the investor would consider a higher equity stake instead of a royalty.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: The investor refuses, stating a royalty aligns their incentives to sell units.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: An investor asks why he will not just take more equity.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: The offering investor points out that the other sharks are not making offers and defends his terms.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder counters again, asking if the investor would accept a 3 dollar royalty.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: The investor refuses, citing their low sales volume.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder argues sales will increase with the investor's help.

turns.speaker: S2

turns.speaker: F1
